prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Sentinel Vale: EO mission (land/coastal/cryosphere). Ground segment plans, acquires, keeps ops safe, generates/archives products, controls access; outside: spacecraft, launch segment, external user processing. Mission Control Center (Bluebell): real-time ops, anomaly response, releases validated commands, owns contact schedule, primary routing policy point; contact = readiness check, live monitoring, post-pass closure; coordinates with PPF on instrument mode/downlink priority/gaps; sends constraints to MPS; receives command preparation package from MPS into command engineering workflow. Spacecraft Ops Team: console lead declares pass status, authorizes commands, pauses on telemetry mismatch; telemetry/systems engineers; uses Antenna Deicing Notice to assess contingency margin. Escalation: console lead > discipline lead > mission management. Possible fault: preserve command state, no discretionary commanding. Command Validation Gateway (Osprey): shall independently validate command stacks (syntax, timing, ranges, sequencing, mode compatibility, schedule baseline); shall reject unapproved manual edits, missing provenance, expired config refs, out-of-authority-window activities; consults Telemetry Ingest Service for spacecraft state, Orbit Determination Engine for orbital solution. Flight Dynamics Facility (Mistral)/Flight Dynamics Team: orbit predictions, visibility, maneuvers; reviews low-margin geometry. Payload Processing Facility (Forgehouse): receives planning metadata (not delivery commitment); Primary/Backup Processing Clusters (failover; capacity check in planning). Payload Calibration Team: Calibration Patch Bundle; reviews calibration activities. Network Control System (Lantern): routing, station allocation, WAN state; sends MCC antenna status, link config, timing. Mission Planning System (Cedar): authoritative timelines; requests via User Services Portal or MCC; admission checks; draft schedule (imaging, recorder, housekeeping, S-band support, X-band downlinks); flags spacecraft/station/staffing conflicts; constraint checks slew, sun-angle, power, thermal, recorder, command load, separation. Telemetry Ingest Service: frames, Pass Replay Packet. Orbit Determination Engine: Doppler Residual Report. Product Quality Service: planning feedback. Long Term Archive (rate-limited during contacts). Ground Network Manager (Juniper): antenna assignment, Antenna Deicing Notice, maintenance-window check before release, Security Exception Ticket to Cybersecurity Desk. Antennas: North/South S-Band; Kiruna/Svalbard X-Band (to PPF). Redundant clocks, PTP, authenticated NTP. Rules: daily

Document units:
S125: The Cybersecurity Desk reviews command preparation exceptions when unusual access, emergency procedure use, or nonstandard transfer paths are requested before uplink.
S126: Final approval requires concurrence from the Mission Control Center and the Spacecraft Operations Team before any command stack is placed in the queue for the next authorized uplink opportunity.
S127: After final command approval, orbit state management remains under continuous control so that operations users work from a common predicted trajectory.
S128: The Orbit Determination Engine fits dynamic orbit solutions using radiometric tracking, spacecraft telemetry timing, force models, and the latest approved maneuver history.
S129: Tracking arcs include measurements associated with the North S-Band Antenna, South S-Band Antenna, Kiruna X-Band Antenna, and Svalbard X-Band Antenna when those data meet quality and timing criteria.
S130: The Product Quality Service checks each orbit solution for frame consistency, covariance reasonableness, time-tag continuity, and agreement with recent contact predictions.
S131: The Flight Dynamics Team uses the residual report to separate station-related tracking biases from dynamic model errors before accepting an orbit solution.
S132: The Flight Dynamics Facility maintains the authoritative orbit catalog for the ground segment and records the modeling assumptions applied to each accepted solution.
S133: Maneuver screening evaluates orbit maintenance options against fuel use, ground contact visibility, payload outage constraints, and post-burn tracking opportunities.
S134: For each candidate burn, the Flight Dynamics Team computes expected state change, execution tolerance, recovery strategy, and the earliest time when the solution can be declared stable.
S135: Collision assessment uses externally supplied conjunction data together with the current covariance to estimate miss distance, encounter geometry, and probability of collision.
S136: The Flight Dynamics Team maintains screening rules that distinguish routine catalog monitoring from events requiring immediate operator notification.
S137: If the predicted risk exceeds the mission threshold, the Spacecraft Operations Team receives a maneuver recommendation package that includes timing constraints and operational impacts.
S138: Attitude geometry support translates the predicted orbit into Sun angle, Earth limb, lunar exclusion, target visibility, and antenna pointing information for daily operations.
S139: The Flight Dynamics Facility sends the Star Tracker Mask File after verifying predicted bright-object exclusions against the current attitude plan.
S140: Bluebell requires that each flight dynamics delivery include a validity interval, coordinate frame, generation time, and operational use statement.
